clue.text: First to film bird of prey getting poultry

indicators.note: the first of a word's letters is the one at its front, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

parts.note: the opening letter of film
an owl hunts small animals at night

explanation.surface: A wildlife cameraman films a hawk that swoops down and grabs a farmyard chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Fowl are domestic birds such as chickens and ducks kept for meat or eggs, which is what poultry means.

clue.text: Defensive structure put around ancient city, advantageous in the long term

indicators.note: something put around another thing encloses it, so the structure wraps the city

parts.note: a fort is a fortified building
Thebes was a city of ancient Egypt and also of Greece

explanation.surface: Building a fortification around an ancient city proves a wise long-term investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for the best turns out well in the end, even if it seems unwelcome at first.

clue.text: Dire warning to a settlers' convoy

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, a state of disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A grave alert is issued to pioneers travelling west together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon train was a line of covered wagons carrying settlers across the American West.

clue.text: Diplomat, American, so sad, drunk in pub

indicators.note: a drunk person's words come out jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: AM is a standard abbreviation for American

indicators.note: being in a place means being held inside it, so the jumbled letters sit within the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a place serving drinks
these five letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: An American envoy, feeling miserable, has had too much to drink in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as the diplomat's condition, but it only scrambles the two little words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador is a senior diplomat representing one country in another.

clue.text: What a bishop may have on in a joint

definitions.text: What a bishop may have on
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bishop's tall ceremonial headdress
second meaning: a corner joint in carpentry with angled cut ends

explanation.surface: A bishop's attire while visiting a seedy nightspot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the pointed headwear of a bishop and the 45-degree corner join used in picture frames.

clue.text: Artist is full of dismay? Just the opposite with this valuation

indicators.text: is full of dismay? Just the opposite
indicators.note: being full of something means holding it, and the reversal of roles means the distress word is the one doing the holding

parts.note: to appal is to dismay or horrify
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter is horrified by the valuation of his work, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' swaps the roles: instead of the artist holding the dismay, the dismay word holds the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an expert assessment of worth, which is what a valuation is.

clue.text: Very exacting employer in club, propping up bar, drinking drop of lager

indicators.note: in a down clue, propping something up means sitting beneath it, fixing which part comes first
drinking means taking in, so the bar word swallows the drop

parts.note: save means except, as in 'all save one'

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so only the opening letter of the drink is taken

parts.note: the first letter of lager
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A demanding boss at his club leans on the bar sipping a lager.
explanation.walkthrough: Bar looks like a counter in a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave-driver is a person who works others very hard, an idiom for a harsh boss.

clue.text: A couple of rooks — one was unable to fly

wordplay.note: to rook is to cheat, which is also to do someone; two of them side by side

explanation.surface: A pair of crows, one of which could not get off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooks look like birds or chess pieces, but here rook is the verb to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo was a flightless bird of Mauritius, extinct since the 17th century.

clue.text: Seldom seen underdone

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lightly cooked, of meat

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a steak nobody orders; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means uncommon and also describes a steak cooked only briefly, still red inside.

clue.text: Supply a Baltic port

parts.note: to rig is to fit out or supply with equipment
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to provision a harbour town on the Baltic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga, capital of Latvia, is a major port on the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: Stage left — snake appears from piece of equipment

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process
L is the usual abbreviation for left
the adder is Britain's venomous snake

explanation.surface: A stage direction: exit left, as a snake emerges from a stage prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepladder is a folding, free-standing ladder, an item of household or workshop equipment.

clue.text: Awfully enraged after manual worker makes a bomb

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters are garbled into a new order

parts.note: a hand is a labourer, as in farmhand
these seven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A furious labourer resorts to making an explosive device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the rearranged word behind the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand grenade is a small explosive device thrown by hand, a type of bomb.

clue.text: Chap landing on bridge gets bravery award

indicators.note: in a down clue, landing on something means sitting above it, so the chap comes first

parts.note: George is any man's name
to bridge a gap is to cross it

explanation.surface: A man who touched down on a bridge receives a medal for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: The George Cross is the highest British civilian award for gallantry.

clue.text: A British nun, lady possibly securing first of tricks in spades

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast, so the nun and lady letters take in the single letter
possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so just the start of the card-game word is used

parts.note: the first letter of tricks

explanation.surface: A British nun, a lady, wins plenty of tricks in the spades suit at bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades looks like the card suit to go with tricks, but 'in spades' is the idiom for in great quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Having something in spades means having lots of it, so abundantly is a fair adverb swap.

clue.text: The nude ran out below

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A streaker dashed out from down below.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath and below both mean situated lower than or beneath something.

clue.text: US writer in digs, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the answer is spelt differently from the word that is spoken

parts.note: an animal digs burrows, and the word is pronounced like the writer's surname

explanation.surface: An American author staying in rented lodgings, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs looks like British slang for lodgings, but here it is a verb: what a rabbit makes.
explanation.definitionFit: William S. Burroughs (and Edgar Rice Burroughs, creator of Tarzan) were American novelists.

clue.text: Plant in European river duck avoided

parts.note: a German is a European

indicators.note: something avoided is kept out, so a letter is taken away from the river's name

parts.note: the Oder is a river on the German-Polish border
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A plant growing in a European river where ducks never go.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a cricket score of zero, shaped like the letter O; dropping it leaves DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a plant of the mint family, genus Teucrium.

clue.text: Name of old boy, one in service

indicators.note: being in a service means being placed inside it, so the earlier letters go within the service abbreviation

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the senior British armed service
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A former pupil's name, recorded as one serving in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' in crosswords often means one of the armed forces, here the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is a common given name, so it is a name in the plain sense.

clue.text: Pole with money, grand from fraud

parts.note: S is the South Pole, or south
tin is old slang for cash
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A Polish man came into a thousand pounds through a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole looks like a Polish person, but it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a confidence trick or swindle, as in the film The Sting.

clue.text: Bearing of vicar, one going round the Spanish church

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so the vicar's title wraps around the Spanish article

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title
el is Spanish for the
an means one, as the indefinite article
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The demeanour of a priest who tours Spanish churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Bearing looks like posture or manner, but it means connection, as in 'has no bearing on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a bearing on a matter has relevance to it: both mean pertinence or connection.

clue.text: In meeting hall, the French elected corporation's treasurer

parts.note: a chamber is a hall where an assembly meets
la is French for the (feminine)
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: At a council meeting in France, a town's finance officer is voted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sits at the front of the hall phrase rather than marking anything enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamberlain is an officer who manages funds, historically the treasurer of a city corporation.

clue.text: Spree, for example, writer fixed up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation for for example
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A writer gets everything sorted after a bout of excess, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a short spell of indulgence, which is what a spree is.

clue.text: Runs into one in Israeli seaport

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so the cricket letter sits inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a person in a harbour town in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre (Akko) is an ancient port city on the northern coast of Israel.

clue.text: Ring North American albatross?

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
N is the abbreviation for North
US means American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A seabird from North America with a ring on its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Albatross looks like the bird, but it means a burden, from the albatross hung round the mariner's neck in Coleridge's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: An albatross around one's neck is a heavy burden, which is what an onus is.

clue.text: US state capital worker is in agreement

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A government employee in an American state capital agrees with policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Concordant describes things that are consistent or in harmony with each other.

clue.text: From this mount you might get stake back

indicators.note: getting something back means reading it the other way, from end to start

parts.note: the ante is a poker player's stake

explanation.surface: A mountaineer could plant a stake back on this summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: read the volcano backwards and you get the stake.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, so it is a mount.

clue.text: Comfortable situation, one appreciated by deliveryman?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a life of financial ease
second meaning, taken literally: a road that is simple to deliver along

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the idiom literally, as a road with no awkward numbering or steep drives.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on easy street is an idiom for living in comfort and affluence.

clue.text: A widely held but false belief covered in a series of letters from Jeremy Thorpe

definitions.text: A widely held but false belief

indicators.text: covered in a series of letters from
indicators.note: covered in a run of letters means the answer is tucked inside the name that follows, spanning both words

parts.note: the end of the first name and start of the surname

explanation.surface: A popular misconception was dealt with in a series of letters written by the Liberal leader Jeremy Thorpe.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Thorpe was a British Liberal Party leader of the 1960s and 70s; 'letters' sounds like his correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a widely believed but untrue idea, a dictionary sense of the word.
